name: Fractora RF

lead: Fractora is a fractional radiofrequency handpiece from InMode, used in clinics for skin tightening, acne scars and oil production. Morpheus8 was later modified from this platform.

Arrays of pins deliver bipolar RF energy into the skin in a fractional pattern, heating tissue to prompt collagen remodeling. Studies are small prospective and retrospective ones, some combining Fractora with other RF treatments such as FaceTite, plus a sebum trial.

paras: It is a clinic treatment, done in a series of sessions and sometimes combined with other RF devices. Results are described as gradual as skin remodels.
Redness, swelling and pinpoint bleeding are commonly reported for RF microneedling. Fractora-specific adverse data were limited in the sources, and it is a clinic-only procedure.

angle.text: Fractora sends fractional RF through pins into the skin, prompting collagen remodeling and less oil for tighter skin and softer acne scars. It preceded Morpheus8 and has been studied in small, mostly early studies.

lead: Fractora is a fractional bipolar radiofrequency (RF) microneedling-type handpiece from InMode, the platform that was later modified into Morpheus8 [1]. It delivers RF energy through arrays of pins into the skin and has been studied for skin laxity, acne scars and oil production [2][3][4].
Published work is mostly small prospective and retrospective studies, some combining Fractora with other RF treatments such as FaceTite.

paras: A 2019 Aesthetic Surgery Journal report examined adjustable-depth fractional RF combined with bipolar RF as a minimally invasive combination for skin laxity, framed around patients too mild for excisional surgery but not for noninvasive devices alone [2].

A retrospective review in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Global Open evaluated a combination of bipolar RF (FaceTite) and fractional bipolar RF (Fractora modified to Morpheus8) for lower face and neck laxity [1].

A 2022 prospective, evaluator-blinded trial measured sebum production after three monthly sessions with a 24-pin Fractora tip and also assessed atrophic acne scars [3]. A registered four-person comparison tested 1,550-nm laser against fractional RF microneedling for acne scars in darker skin [4].
Adverse-event details specific to Fractora were not available in the sources reviewed. General RF microneedling risks reported for Morpheus8 include redness, swelling and pinpoint bleeding [5].
